fieldMarks: 15-17 in; small duck with a short bill.
Male: slaty blue with an intricate white pattern and reddish sides.
Female: dark brown with two or three white face spots; smaller and much shorter-billed than scoters.
Call a mouse-like squeak and low whistles.
behavior: Swims and dives against the current of rushing rivers and climbs on slippery rocks.
Pairs flying inland follow every bend of the river rather than cutting overland.
Mostly a short-distance migrant from inland nesting streams to nearby coasts.
Feeds by diving and walking on the bottom, prying mollusks and crustaceans off rocks; eats aquatic insects on rivers.
habitat: Nests along shallow, fast-moving rivers and streams, often in forested country, generally not on glacier-fed streams.
Winters on exposed rocky ocean coasts where surf pounds, seldom on sheltered bays.
range: Breeds in Alaska, western Canada and the northern Rockies and in eastern Canada; winters along the Pacific coast and the North Atlantic coast from eastern Canada to New England and the Mid-Atlantic.

lookalikes.name: Bufflehead (female)
lookalikes.howToTell: Audubon lists female bufflehead and female scaup as comparison species; female harlequin is dark brown with two or three white face spots.
